text: Eight in the morning, September second. Six T T C elevators are reported out, one of them at Bloor-Yonge.
Union to Bloor-Yonge, step-free. Nineteen minutes becomes thirty.
happy map plans a walk by what it costs your body: the minutes in the cold, the metres in full sun, the stairs, and the elevator that is out right now.
Every route sits beside the fastest one, so you can see what you're trading.
Scotiabank Arena to the Eaton Centre. Sixteen metres outdoors instead of a kilometre. One minute longer.
Shade comes from the city's building model and more than six hundred thousand street trees. When the sky clouds over, the weight on shade eases off.
OpenStreetMap had no sidewalk on half the network. The city's own inventory found one on four and a half thousand kilometres of it.
The elevator feed has been logged every five minutes since September first. Scrub back to a moment, and the routes use the outages recorded then.
One in four step-free trips passes through Bloor-Yonge. Block it, and the median detour is thirty minutes.
None of this is Toronto-only. In Montréal, the same router finds the RÉSO and cuts downtown outdoor walking by a third.
These routes are simulated. No one has tested them on a journey yet.
Eight in the morning, September second. Six elevators out. The detour was on the map before you left.
